Maya (ML Eng): quick sync — proposing a lightweight microbench stage in the model onboarding pipeline to capture kv-cache warmup curves, per-token latency distributions, and small-binary compatibility checks. low-cost probe before full bench. thoughts?

Jun Park: +1. can you sketch where it sits relative to smoke and full bench? i.e., replace anything or sit upstream?

Maya (ML Eng): sits upstream of full bench, downstream of basic ingest/sanity. not a replacement for smoke. goal: cheap (~minutes), stratified seq lengths, produce a small artifact used by runtime for kernel selection / initial batch hints.

Priya Rao: sounds useful. main concern is cost and churn. how often do we run it? every model upload, version change, cron?

Maya (ML Eng): plan = run on every model upload and weekly for pinned models. run duration ~5–10 min per model if we limit reps and sequences. estimate per-model infra cost < $2 if we throttle concurrency.

Ethan G.: we should also use microbench to sanity-check different binaries (fp16 vs quant) and ONNX exports. cheap fidelity check on golden inputs (logit delta threshold) prevents onboarding bad binaries.

Jun Park: agreed. runtime needs two hooks: (1) read microbench artifact for kernel selection, (2) fallback policy when measured p95 > SLA. i'll add a runtime hook RFC item.

Maya (ML Eng): basic proto config I had in mind:

```
microbench:
  seqs: [16, 64, 512]
  reps: 8
  compare_binaries: true
  golden_inputs: samples/quick_golden.json
  thresholds:
    logit_delta: 1e-3
    p95_ms: 75
```

Priya Rao: nice. also add a `max_gpu_minutes` cap so cost is bounded.

Ethan G.: for binary comparison, let's store small per-token statistics (mean abs delta, max delta) not full logits to reduce artifact size. attach script to produce the summary.

onboard-bot: run 1789997001: microbench pass for model `tiny-xl-v2` (artifact: s3://redwood-onboard/microbench/1789997001-summary.json) :white_check_mark:

Maya (ML Eng): action items: I'll draft RFC with example artifacts + cost calc. Jun will add runtime hook. Priya will estimate infra cost and concurrency limits. Ethan will prototype golden-compare script.

Priya Rao: ack, will throw a rough estimate by EOD tomorrow.

Jun Park: i'll stub runtime hook PR next week.

Ethan G.: i'll push a small script to tools/quick-compare and wire into microbench job.

Maya (ML Eng): thanks all — if nobody objects i'll post RFC in docs repo tomorrow. :thumbsup:
